#In brief

  • The exponential function y=axy = a^xy=ax makes sense only with base a>0a > 0a>0 and a≠1a \neq 1a=1. It is always positive, passes through the point (0,1)(0, 1)(0,1), increases if a>1a > 1a>1 and decreases if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1.
  • The logarithm log⁡ab\log_a bloga​b is the exponent you must give the base aaa to obtain bbb: saying log⁡ab=y\log_a b = yloga​b=y is the same as saying ay=ba^y = bay=b. It exists only if a>0a > 0a>0, a≠1a \neq 1a=1 and b>0b > 0b>0.
  • The properties of logarithms turn products into sums, quotients into differences and powers into factors; the change of base brings any logarithm to the base you prefer. For log⁡a(x+y)\log_a(x + y)loga​(x+y) there is no rule at all.
  • ln⁡\lnln denotes the logarithm to base eee (natural logarithm; eee is an irrational number approximately equal to 2.7182.7182.718), log⁡10\log_{10}log10​ the logarithm to base 10.
  • Exponential and logarithm with the same base are inverse functions: their graphs are symmetric with respect to the line y=xy = xy=x.
  • Exponential equations: with the same base, set the exponents equal; otherwise, switch to logarithms. Logarithmic equations: first the domain conditions, then the calculations, and at the end discard the solutions that are not acceptable.
  • Inequalities: with a base greater than 1 the direction stays the same, with a base between 0 and 1 the direction is reversed. In logarithmic inequalities the result must be put in a system with the domain conditions.

#7.1 Exponentials and logarithms

#From powers to real exponents

A power ana^nan is a short way to write a product: 23=2⋅2⋅2=82^3 = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 823=2⋅2⋅2=8. The number aaa is called the base, the number nnn is called the exponent. To build the exponential function you need to give a meaning to axa^xax for every real exponent xxx: negative, fractional or irrational ones too. The meaning is built in stages, so that the rules for powers always remain valid.

ExponentMeaningExample
natural number n≥1n \geq 1n≥1product of nnn factors equal to aaa23=82^3 = 823=8
zeroa0=1a^0 = 1a0=1 (with a≠0a \neq 0a=0)50=15^0 = 150=1
negative integera−n=1ana^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}a−n=an1​2−3=182^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{8}2−3=81​
fraction mn\dfrac{m}{n}nm​am/n=amna^{m/n} = \sqrt[n]{a^m}am/n=nam​82/3=643=48^{2/3} = \sqrt[3]{64} = 482/3=364​=4
irrationalthe exponent is approximated by fractions closer and closer to it22≈2.672^{\sqrt{2}} \approx 2.6722​≈2.67

Here an\sqrt[n]{a}na​ is the nnn-th root of aaa and the symbol ≈\approx≈ reads “approximately equal to”.

Why the base must be positive. With exponent 12\frac{1}{2}21​ you have a1/2=aa^{1/2} = \sqrt{a}a1/2=a​: if aaa were negative, for example a=−4a = -4a=−4, you would have to compute −4\sqrt{-4}−4​, which does not exist in the real numbers. That is why the exponential function always requires a>0a > 0a>0; a=0a = 0a=0 is left out too, because 0−1=100^{-1} = \frac{1}{0}0−1=01​ does not exist. The base a=1a = 1a=1 is excluded as well: 1x=11^x = 11x=1 for every xxx, and you would get a constant function, always equal to 1. With a positive base the result is always positive: ax>0a^x > 0ax>0 for every xxx.

  • 272/3=(273)2=32=927^{2/3} = \left(\sqrt[3]{27}\right)^2 = 3^2 = 9272/3=(327​)2=32=9. It pays to take the root first: the numbers stay small.

Common mistake Mistakes with powers
  • A negative exponent turns the number upside down, it does not change the sign: 2−3=182^{-3} = \frac{1}{8}2−3=81​, not −8-8−8.
  • am+na^{m+n}am+n is not am+ana^m + a^nam+an: 21+2=82^{1+2} = 821+2=8, while 21+22=62^1 + 2^2 = 621+22=6.
  • −22=−4-2^2 = -4−22=−4 (the minus stays outside the power), while (−2)2=4(-2)^2 = 4(−2)2=4.
Note Power or exponential?

In y=x2y = x^2y=x2 the variable is in the base and the exponent is fixed: it is a power function. In y=2xy = 2^xy=2x the base is fixed and the variable is in the exponent: it is an exponential function. They are very different functions. For example 32=93^2 = 932=9 is bigger than 23=82^3 = 823=8, but 102=10010^2 = 100102=100 is much smaller than 210=10242^{10} = 1024210=1024: as you go further, the exponential overtakes any power.

#The exponential function

Definition 7.1 Exponential function

Given a number aaa with a>0a > 0a>0 and a≠1a \neq 1a=1, the exponential function with base aaa is the function f(x)=axf(x) = a^xf(x)=ax, which assigns to every real number xxx the number axa^xax.

Rule 7.2 Features of y=axy = a^xy=ax
  • Domain: all of R\RR, the set of real numbers: every xxx is allowed.
  • Sign: ax>0a^x > 0ax>0 always; the range (image) is the interval (0,+∞)(0, +\infty)(0,+∞), where the symbol ∞\infty∞ reads “infinity”.
  • Key points: the graph always passes through (0,1)(0, 1)(0,1), because a0=1a^0 = 1a0=1, and through (1,a)(1, a)(1,a), because a1=aa^1 = aa1=a.
  • Monotonicity: if a>1a > 1a>1 the function is increasing, if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1 it is decreasing. In both cases it is monotonic, so au=ava^u = a^vau=av only when u=vu = vu=v.
  • Asymptote: the graph approaches the xxx-axis without ever touching it (the xxx-axis is a horizontal asymptote): towards the left if a>1a > 1a>1, towards the right if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1.

The two graphs are symmetric with respect to the yyy-axis: indeed (12)x=2−x\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^x = 2^{-x}(21​)x=2−x, so the value of (12)x\left(\frac12\right)^x(21​)x at x=3x = 3x=3 is equal to the value of 2x2^x2x at x=−3x = -3x=−3.

Rule 7.3 Comparing two powers with the same base
  • If a>1a > 1a>1: au<ava^u < a^vau<av exactly when u<vu < vu<v (the order of the exponents is preserved).
  • If 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1: au<ava^u < a^vau<av exactly when u>vu > vu>v (the order is reversed).

In symbols, for a>1a > 1a>1 you write au<av  ⟺  u<va^u < a^v \iff u < vau<av⟺u<v, where   ⟺  \iff⟺ reads “if and only if”.

Example 7.2 Comparisons without a calculator
  • 20.32^{0.3}20.3 and 20.52^{0.5}20.5: the base 2 is greater than 1 and 0.3<0.50.3 < 0.50.3<0.5, so 20.3<20.52^{0.3} < 2^{0.5}20.3<20.5.
  • (13)0.3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{0.3}(31​)0.3 and (13)0.5\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{0.5}(31​)0.5: the base is between 0 and 1, so the order is reversed: (13)0.3>(13)0.5\left(\frac13\right)^{0.3} > \left(\frac13\right)^{0.5}(31​)0.3>(31​)0.5.
  • 2302^{30}230 and 3203^{20}320: the bases are different, but the exponents have the common divisor 10. 230=(23)10=8102^{30} = (2^3)^{10} = 8^{10}230=(23)10=810 and 320=(32)10=9103^{20} = (3^2)^{10} = 9^{10}320=(32)10=910. With the same positive exponent the larger base wins: 810<9108^{10} < 9^{10}810<910, so 230<3202^{30} < 3^{20}230<320.

#The logarithm

The equation 2x=82^x = 82x=8 can be solved by inspection: x=3x = 3x=3. But what about 2x=52^x = 52x=5? The exponent you are looking for lies between 2 and 3, because 22=4<5<8=232^2 = 4 < 5 < 8 = 2^322=4<5<8=23, and it is not a “simple” number. It is given a name: it is the logarithm of 5 to base 2, and it is written log⁡25\log_2 5log2​5.

Definition 7.2 Logarithm

Let a>0a > 0a>0 with a≠1a \neq 1a=1, and b>0b > 0b>0. The logarithm of bbb to base aaa, written log⁡ab\log_a bloga​b, is the exponent to which you must raise aaa to obtain bbb:

log⁡ab=y  ⟺  ay=b\log_a b = y \iff a^y = bloga​b=y⟺ay=b

The number aaa is the base, the number bbb is the argument of the logarithm.

The conditions on the base are the same as for exponentials. The argument must be positive because aya^yay is always positive: no exponent turns aaa into zero or into a negative number.

Method Computing a logarithm by hand
  1. Write the base and the argument as powers of the same number: a=cma = c^ma=cm and b=cnb = c^nb=cn.
  2. You are looking for yyy with ay=ba^y = bay=b, that is cmy=cnc^{my} = c^ncmy=cn: the exponents must be equal, my=nmy = nmy=n.
  3. So log⁡ab=nm\log_a b = \dfrac{n}{m}loga​b=mn​. Always check backwards: aaa raised to the result must give bbb.
Example 7.3 Logarithms computed from the definition
  • log⁡381=4\log_3 81 = 4log3​81=4, because 34=813^4 = 8134=81.
  • log⁡218=−3\log_2 \frac{1}{8} = -3log2​81​=−3, because 2−3=182^{-3} = \frac{1}{8}2−3=81​.
  • log⁡1/28=−3\log_{1/2} 8 = -3log1/2​8=−3, because (12)−3=23=8\left(\frac12\right)^{-3} = 2^3 = 8(21​)−3=23=8.
  • log⁡93=12\log_9 3 = \frac{1}{2}log9​3=21​, because 91/2=9=39^{1/2} = \sqrt{9} = 391/2=9​=3.
  • log⁡48\log_4 8log4​8: 4=224 = 2^24=22 and 8=238 = 2^38=23, so log⁡48=32\log_4 8 = \frac{3}{2}log4​8=23​. Check: 43/2=(4)3=84^{3/2} = \left(\sqrt{4}\right)^3 = 843/2=(4​)3=8.
  • log⁡1/432\log_{1/4} 32log1/4​32: 14=2−2\frac14 = 2^{-2}41​=2−2 and 32=2532 = 2^532=25, so log⁡1/432=5−2=−52\log_{1/4} 32 = \frac{5}{-2} = -\frac{5}{2}log1/4​32=−25​=−25​.
  • log⁡100.01=−2\log_{10} 0.01 = -2log10​0.01=−2, because 10−2=1100=0.0110^{-2} = \frac{1}{100} = 0.0110−2=1001​=0.01.
  • log⁡39=4\log_{\sqrt{3}} 9 = 4log3​​9=4, because (3)4=32=9\left(\sqrt{3}\right)^4 = 3^2 = 9(3​)4=32=9.
Rule 7.4 Four equalities to know by heart

For every allowed base aaa:

  • log⁡a1=0\log_a 1 = 0loga​1=0, because a0=1a^0 = 1a0=1;
  • log⁡aa=1\log_a a = 1loga​a=1, because a1=aa^1 = aa1=a;
  • log⁡aax=x\log_a a^x = xloga​ax=x for every real xxx: the logarithm “undoes” the power;
  • alog⁡ax=xa^{\log_a x} = xaloga​x=x for every x>0x > 0x>0: the power “undoes” the logarithm.
Example 7.4 Using the four equalities
  • 5log⁡57=75^{\log_5 7} = 75log5​7=7 and log⁡33−4=−4\log_3 3^{-4} = -4log3​3−4=−4.
  • 23+log⁡25=23⋅2log⁡25=8⋅5=402^{3 + \log_2 5} = 2^3 \cdot 2^{\log_2 5} = 8 \cdot 5 = 4023+log2​5=23⋅2log2​5=8⋅5=40.
  • 102log⁡103=(10log⁡103)2=32=910^{2\log_{10} 3} = \left(10^{\log_{10} 3}\right)^2 = 3^2 = 9102log10​3=(10log10​3)2=32=9.
Common mistake What does not exist
  • The logarithm of zero or of a negative number does not exist: log⁡2(−4)\log_2(-4)log2​(−4) and log⁡30\log_3 0log3​0 make no sense. The result of a logarithm, on the other hand, can be negative or zero: log⁡212=−1\log_2 \frac12 = -1log2​21​=−1, log⁡71=0\log_7 1 = 0log7​1=0.
  • Base 1 is not allowed, and neither is a negative base.
  • log⁡ab\log_a bloga​b and log⁡ba\log_b alogb​a are in general different numbers, each the reciprocal of the other: log⁡28=3\log_2 8 = 3log2​8=3, while log⁡82=13\log_8 2 = \frac13log8​2=31​.

#The properties of logarithms

The properties of logarithms are the properties of powers read from the point of view of the exponents. If x=amx = a^mx=am and y=any = a^ny=an, then xy=am+nxy = a^{m+n}xy=am+n: so log⁡a(xy)=m+n=log⁡ax+log⁡ay\log_a(xy) = m + n = \log_a x + \log_a yloga​(xy)=m+n=loga​x+loga​y. When you multiply two powers the exponents add up, and a logarithm is precisely an exponent.

Note Why the absolute value sometimes appears

The formulas require positive arguments. If xxx and yyy are both negative, the product xyxyxy is positive and log⁡a(xy)\log_a(xy)loga​(xy) exists, while log⁡ax\log_a xloga​x and log⁡ay\log_a yloga​y do not. #The bases eee and 10

Two bases are used more than all the others, and they are the ones you find on calculators.

Euler's number eee (Napier's constant) is an irrational number: e≈2.71828e \approx 2.71828e≈2.71828. The logarithm to base eee is called the natural logarithm (or Napierian logarithm) and is written ln⁡x\ln xlnx, without indicating the base. So ln⁡e=1\ln e = 1lne=1, ln⁡1=0\ln 1 = 0ln1=0, ln⁡e3=3\ln e^3 = 3lne3=3 and eln⁡5=5e^{\ln 5} = 5eln5=5. The base eee has a handy property: when yyy is close to zero,

ln⁡(1+y)≈y\ln(1 + y) \approx yln(1+y)≈y

For example ln⁡1.01≈0.01\ln 1.01 \approx 0.01ln1.01≈0.01 (the true value is 0.00995…0.00995\ldots0.00995…).

The logarithm to base 10 is called the common logarithm (or decimal logarithm). In many books and on calculators it is written just log⁡\loglog; here we always write the base, log⁡10\log_{10}log10​. On powers of 10 it is computed straight away: log⁡101000=3\log_{10} 1000 = 3log10​1000=3 and log⁡100.001=−3\log_{10} 0.001 = -3log10​0.001=−3.

Note Scientific notation: characteristic and mantissa

Every positive number can be written in scientific notation, x=m⋅10kx = m \cdot 10^kx=m⋅10k with 1≤m<101 \leq m < 101≤m<10 and kkk an integer. Then

log⁡10x=k+log⁡10m,0≤log⁡10m<1\log_{10} x = k + \log_{10} m, \qquad 0 \leq \log_{10} m < 1log10​x=k+log10​m,0≤log10​m<1

The integer part kkk is called the characteristic, the fractional part log⁡10m\log_{10} mlog10​m is called the mantissa. Example: 4500=4.5⋅1034500 = 4.5 \cdot 10^34500=4.5⋅103, so log⁡104500=3+log⁡104.5≈3+0.653=3.653\log_{10} 4500 = 3 + \log_{10} 4.5 \approx 3 + 0.653 = 3.653log10​4500=3+log10​4.5≈3+0.653=3.653. And 45=4.5⋅10145 = 4.5 \cdot 10^145=4.5⋅101 gives log⁡1045≈1.653\log_{10} 45 \approx 1.653log10​45≈1.653: same digits, same mantissa, only the characteristic changes. This works only in base 10. Practical consequence: if a number greater than or equal to 1 has nnn digits before the decimal point, its common logarithm is at least n−1n - 1n−1 and less than nnn.

Calculators usually have keys only for ln⁡\lnln and for the base-10 logarithm: the other bases are obtained with the change of base, for example log⁡37=ln⁡7ln⁡3\log_3 7 = \dfrac{\ln 7}{\ln 3}log3​7=ln3ln7​. In the test there is no calculator, so a number like log⁡37\log_3 7log3​7 stays written like that, or in the equivalent form ln⁡7ln⁡3\dfrac{\ln 7}{\ln 3}ln3ln7​.

#The logarithmic function

Definition 7.3 Logarithmic function

Given a>0a > 0a>0 with a≠1a \neq 1a=1, the logarithmic function with base aaa is the function f(x)=log⁡axf(x) = \log_a xf(x)=loga​x, defined for x>0x > 0x>0.

Rule 7.6 Features of y=log⁡axy = \log_a xy=loga​x
  • Domain: (0,+∞)(0, +\infty)(0,+∞): only positive arguments.
  • Range: all of R\RR.
  • Key points: the graph passes through (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0), because log⁡a1=0\log_a 1 = 0loga​1=0, and through (a,1)(a, 1)(a,1).
  • Monotonicity: increasing if a>1a > 1a>1, decreasing if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1.
  • Asymptote: the yyy-axis is a vertical asymptote: near x=0x = 0x=0 the graph goes down towards −∞-\infty−∞ if a>1a > 1a>1 and up towards +∞+\infty+∞ if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1.
  • Sign: if a>1a > 1a>1, log⁡ax\log_a xloga​x is negative for 0<x<10 < x < 10<x<1 and positive for x>1x > 1x>1; if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1 the opposite happens.

Here too the two graphs are symmetric, this time with respect to the xxx-axis: with the change of base, log⁡1/2x=log⁡2xlog⁡212=−log⁡2x\log_{1/2} x = \dfrac{\log_2 x}{\log_2 \frac12} = -\log_2 xlog1/2​x=log2​21​log2​x​=−log2​x.

Method Domain of a function with logarithms
  1. Write the condition “argument >0> 0>0” for each logarithm, with a strict “greater than”.
  2. Add the other conditions: denominators different from zero, radicands of even-index roots greater than or equal to zero.
  3. Solve the system: the domain is the set of values that satisfy all the conditions at the same time.
Example 7.6 Domains
  • f(x)=log⁡2(x−3)f(x) = \log_2(x - 3)f(x)=log2​(x−3): you need x−3>0x - 3 > 0x−3>0, domain (3,+∞)(3, +\infty)(3,+∞).
  • f(x)=ln⁡(4−x2)f(x) = \ln(4 - x^2)f(x)=ln(4−x2): you need 4−x2>04 - x^2 > 04−x2>0, that is x2<4x^2 < 4x2<4, domain (−2,2)(-2, 2)(−2,2).
  • f(x)=ln⁡(x2+1)f(x) = \ln(x^2 + 1)f(x)=ln(x2+1): x2+1x^2 + 1x2+1 is always positive, domain R\RR.
  • f(x)=log⁡3x+1x−2f(x) = \log_3 \dfrac{x + 1}{x - 2}f(x)=log3​x−2x+1​: you need x+1x−2>0\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 2} > 0x−2x+1​>0. The numerator is positive for x>−1x > -1x>−1, the denominator for x>2x > 2x>2; the fraction is positive when they have the same sign, that is for x<−1x < -1x<−1 or x>2x > 2x>2. Domain (−∞,−1)∪(2,+∞)(-\infty, -1) \cup (2, +\infty)(−∞,−1)∪(2,+∞), where ∪\cup∪ denotes the union.

#Exponential and logarithm are inverse functions

Rule 7.7 Inverse functions

With the same base aaa:

log⁡a(ax)=x  for every x∈R,alog⁡ax=x  for every x>0\log_a\left(a^x\right) = x \ \text{ for every } x \in \R, \qquad a^{\log_a x} = x \ \text{ for every } x > 0loga​(ax)=x  for every x∈R,aloga​x=x  for every x>0

(∈\in∈ reads “belongs to”). Each function undoes the other: y=axy = a^xy=ax and y=log⁡axy = \log_a xy=loga​x are inverse functions. Their graphs are symmetric with respect to the line y=xy = xy=x, the bisector of the first and third quadrants: if the point (p,q)(p, q)(p,q) lies on the graph of the exponential, the point (q,p)(q, p)(q,p) lies on the graph of the logarithm.

y=axy = a^xy=axy=log⁡axy = \log_a xy=loga​x
domainR\RR(0,+∞)(0, +\infty)(0,+∞)
range(0,+∞)(0, +\infty)(0,+∞)R\RR
passes through(0,1)(0, 1)(0,1) and (1,a)(1, a)(1,a)(1,0)(1, 0)(1,0) and (a,1)(a, 1)(a,1)
asymptotexxx-axis (horizontal)yyy-axis (vertical)
monotonicityincreasing if a>1a > 1a>1, decreasing if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1the same as the exponential

Domain and range swap, as always happens between a function and its inverse.

#Exponential models

Many phenomena grow or shrink by the same percentage at regular time intervals: a population of bacteria, invested capital, a radioactive substance that decays. At each interval the quantity is multiplied by the same factor qqq, so after ttt intervals

N(t)=N0⋅qtN(t) = N_0 \cdot q^tN(t)=N0​⋅qt

where N0N_0N0​ is the initial quantity. If q>1q > 1q>1 the quantity grows, if 0<q<10 < q < 10<q<1 it decreases.

  • An increase of p%p\%p% at each step: q=1+p100q = 1 + \frac{p}{100}q=1+100p​. For example an increase of 10%10\%10% per year gives q=1.1q = 1.1q=1.1.
  • A decrease of p%p\%p% at each step: q=1−p100q = 1 - \frac{p}{100}q=1−100p​.
  • Doubling at each step: q=2q = 2q=2; halving: q=12q = \frac12q=21​.
Example 7.7 Bacteria that double

A bacterium splits in two every hour. Starting from a single bacterium you have 1,2,4,8,…1, 2, 4, 8, \ldots1,2,4,8,… bacteria: after ttt hours there are N(t)=2tN(t) = 2^tN(t)=2t, and after 10 hours there are 210=10242^{10} = 1024210=1024.

If there are 3 bacteria at the start, the model is N(t)=3⋅2tN(t) = 3 \cdot 2^tN(t)=3⋅2t. When does the number go above 1000 bacteria? You need 3⋅2t>10003 \cdot 2^t > 10003⋅2t>1000, that is 2t>10003≈3332^t > \frac{1000}{3} \approx 3332t>31000​≈333. Since 28=2562^8 = 25628=256 and 29=5122^9 = 51229=512, counting whole hours the 1000 mark is passed after 9 hours: 3⋅28=7683 \cdot 2^8 = 7683⋅28=768, while 3⋅29=15363 \cdot 2^9 = 15363⋅29=1536.

Example 7.8 Radioactive decay

A radioactive substance halves every 5 years. After ttt years, M(t)=M0(12)t/5M(t) = M_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/5}M(t)=M0​(21​)t/5 of it remains, where M0M_0M0​ is the initial quantity. After 15 years the exponent is 155=3\frac{15}{5} = 3515​=3: (12)3=18\left(\frac12\right)^3 = \frac18(21​)3=81​ of the initial quantity remains.

Note The limits of the model

In reality no population grows exponentially forever: food, space and other resources are limited. These limiting factors slow growth down until it levels off or stops. The exponential model describes a phenomenon well only for a limited period.

In the test Exponentials and logarithms in the test questions
  • Computing logarithms (numeric answer or one option out of four): write base and argument as powers of the same number and check backwards, raising the base to the result.
  • True or false on the properties: if you do not remember a formula, test it with simple numbers (base 2, arguments 4 and 8). A single counterexample is enough to answer “false”.
  • Estimates without a calculator: log⁡210\log_2 10log2​10 is between 3 and 4, because 23=8<10<16=242^3 = 8 < 10 < 16 = 2^423=8<10<16=24. An estimate like this is often enough to discard the wrong options.
  • Recognising graphs: the graph of y=axy = a^xy=ax passes through (0,1)(0, 1)(0,1) and lies entirely above the xxx-axis; that of y=log⁡axy = \log_a xy=loga​x passes through (1,0)(1, 0)(1,0) and lies entirely to the right of the yyy-axis. If the graph goes down, the base is between 0 and 1.
  • Domain: the argument of every logarithm must be strictly positive; then take the values that satisfy all the conditions.

#7.2 Exponential and logarithmic equations and inequalities

Equations and inequalities in which the unknown is in the exponent or in the argument of a logarithm are called transcendental: they are not algebraic like those of modules 3 and 4. All the methods rely on two facts seen above: exponentials and logarithms are monotonic functions (so they give the same value only with the same exponent or the same argument), and each is the inverse of the other.

#Exponential equations

In an exponential equation the unknown appears in the exponent. The conditions on the bases (a>0a > 0a>0, a≠1a \neq 1a=1) are taken for granted. Below, f(x)f(x)f(x) and g(x)g(x)g(x) denote expressions that contain xxx.

Method The four typical cases
  1. Same base: af(x)=ag(x)  ⟺  f(x)=g(x)a^{f(x)} = a^{g(x)} \iff f(x) = g(x)af(x)=ag(x)⟺f(x)=g(x). Often you first need to write everything as a power of the same base (4=224 = 2^24=22, 19=3−2\frac19 = 3^{-2}91​=3−2, 5=51/2\sqrt{5} = 5^{1/2}5​=51/2).
  2. Exponential equal to a number: af(x)=ca^{f(x)} = caf(x)=c. If c≤0c \leq 0c≤0 the equation is impossible. If c>0c > 0c>0, apply log⁡a\log_aloga​ to both sides: f(x)=log⁡acf(x) = \log_a cf(x)=loga​c.
  3. Different bases: af(x)=bg(x)a^{f(x)} = b^{g(x)}af(x)=bg(x). Apply the same logarithm to both sides (for example ln⁡\lnln): f(x)ln⁡a=g(x)ln⁡bf(x)\ln a = g(x)\ln bf(x)lna=g(x)lnb, and solve.
  4. Equations that can be reduced: take out a common power, or set t=axt = a^xt=ax (with t>0t > 0t>0) and solve an algebraic equation in ttt.
Example 7.9 Same base
  • 4x+1=8x4^{x+1} = 8^x4x+1=8x. Everything in base 2: 4x+1=(22)x+1=22x+24^{x+1} = \left(2^2\right)^{x+1} = 2^{2x+2}4x+1=(22)x+1=22x+2 and 8x=23x8^x = 2^{3x}8x=23x. So 2x+2=3x2x + 2 = 3x2x+2=3x, that is x=2x = 2x=2. Check: 43=644^3 = 6443=64 and 82=648^2 = 6482=64.
  • (13)x=9x−3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x = 9^{x-3}(31​)x=9x−3. Everything in base 3: 3−x=32x−63^{-x} = 3^{2x-6}3−x=32x−6, so −x=2x−6-x = 2x - 6−x=2x−6 and x=2x = 2x=2.
  • 2x2−3x=142^{x^2 - 3x} = \frac{1}{4}2x2−3x=41​. Since 14=2−2\frac14 = 2^{-2}41​=2−2: x2−3x=−2x^2 - 3x = -2x2−3x=−2, that is x2−3x+2=0x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0x2−3x+2=0, with solutions x=1x = 1x=1 and x=2x = 2x=2.
Example 7.10 Exponential equal to a number
  • 5x+1=75^{x+1} = 75x+1=7: x+1=log⁡57x + 1 = \log_5 7x+1=log5​7, so x=log⁡57−1x = \log_5 7 - 1x=log5​7−1.
  • e2x−1=3e^{2x-1} = 3e2x−1=3: 2x−1=ln⁡32x - 1 = \ln 32x−1=ln3, so x=1+ln⁡32x = \dfrac{1 + \ln 3}{2}x=21+ln3​.
  • 6x+3=16^{x+3} = 16x+3=1: 1=601 = 6^01=60, so x+3=0x + 3 = 0x+3=0 and x=−3x = -3x=−3. Equal to 1 does not mean impossible.
  • 32x=−93^{2x} = -932x=−9: impossible, because an exponential is never negative.
Example 7.11 Different bases

3x=2x+13^x = 2^{x+1}3x=2x+1. Apply ln⁡\lnln to both sides and use the power property:

xln⁡3=(x+1)ln⁡2  ⇒  xln⁡3−xln⁡2=ln⁡2  ⇒  x=ln⁡2ln⁡3−ln⁡2=ln⁡2ln⁡32x\ln 3 = (x + 1)\ln 2 \;\Rightarrow\; x\ln 3 - x\ln 2 = \ln 2 \;\Rightarrow\; x = \frac{\ln 2}{\ln 3 - \ln 2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\ln \frac{3}{2}}xln3=(x+1)ln2⇒xln3−xln2=ln2⇒x=ln3−ln2ln2​=ln23​ln2​

The symbol ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ reads “therefore”. You could also divide by 2x2^x2x: (32)x=2\left(\frac32\right)^x = 2(23​)x=2, that is x=log⁡3/22x = \log_{3/2} 2x=log3/2​2. It is the same number written in another form: among the options of a question the solution can appear in any of these forms.

Example 7.12 Taking out a common factor and substitution
  • 2x+2−2x=242^{x+2} - 2^x = 242x+2−2x=24. Since 2x+2=4⋅2x2^{x+2} = 4 \cdot 2^x2x+2=4⋅2x, take out 2x2^x2x: 2x(4−1)=242^x(4 - 1) = 242x(4−1)=24, so 2x=82^x = 82x=8 and x=3x = 3x=3.
  • 4x−6⋅2x+8=04^x - 6 \cdot 2^x + 8 = 04x−6⋅2x+8=0. Since 4x=(2x)24^x = \left(2^x\right)^24x=(2x)2, set t=2xt = 2^xt=2x: t2−6t+8=0t^2 - 6t + 8 = 0t2−6t+8=0, with solutions t=2t = 2t=2 and t=4t = 4t=4. Back to xxx: 2x=22^x = 22x=2 gives x=1x = 1x=1, 2x=42^x = 42x=4 gives x=2x = 2x=2.
  • 9x+3x−12=09^x + 3^x - 12 = 09x+3x−12=0. With t=3xt = 3^xt=3x: t2+t−12=0t^2 + t - 12 = 0t2+t−12=0, with solutions t=3t = 3t=3 and t=−4t = -4t=−4. The value t=−4t = -4t=−4 is discarded (3x3^x3x is always positive), so what remains is 3x=33^x = 33x=3, that is x=1x = 1x=1.
Common mistake Mistakes in exponential equations
  • 2x+2x=2⋅2x=2x+12^x + 2^x = 2 \cdot 2^x = 2^{x+1}2x+2x=2⋅2x=2x+1: it is not 22x2^{2x}22x.
  • You can set the exponents equal only when each side is a single power of the same base. In 2x+2=82^x + 2 = 82x+2=8 you cannot “drop the base”: first isolate the power, 2x=62^x = 62x=6, and then x=log⁡26x = \log_2 6x=log2​6.
  • After the substitution t=axt = a^xt=ax you must go back to xxx: the values of ttt are not the solutions.

#Logarithmic equations

In a logarithmic equation the unknown appears in the argument of one or more logarithms.

Method Solving a logarithmic equation
  1. Domain conditions (C.E. for short, from the Italian condizioni di esistenza): every argument must be greater than zero. Write them for the original equation, before any transformation.
  2. Using the properties, you reach one of these two forms:
    • log⁡af(x)=c\log_a f(x) = cloga​f(x)=c: by the definition of logarithm, f(x)=acf(x) = a^cf(x)=ac;
    • log⁡af(x)=log⁡ag(x)\log_a f(x) = \log_a g(x)loga​f(x)=loga​g(x): the arguments must be equal, f(x)=g(x)f(x) = g(x)f(x)=g(x).
  3. Solve the resulting algebraic equation.
  4. Keep only the solutions that satisfy the C.E.
Example 7.13 The two basic forms
  • log⁡3(2x+1)=2\log_3(2x + 1) = 2log3​(2x+1)=2. C.E.: 2x+1>02x + 1 > 02x+1>0, that is x>−12x > -\frac12x>−21​. By the definition 2x+1=32=92x + 1 = 3^2 = 92x+1=32=9, so x=4x = 4x=4: it satisfies the C.E., so it is acceptable.
  • ln⁡(x−1)=2\ln(x - 1) = 2ln(x−1)=2. C.E.: x>1x > 1x>1. By the definition x−1=e2x - 1 = e^2x−1=e2, so x=1+e2x = 1 + e^2x=1+e2 (about 8.398.398.39): acceptable.
  • log⁡2(x+3)=log⁡2(2x−1)\log_2(x + 3) = \log_2(2x - 1)log2​(x+3)=log2​(2x−1). C.E.: x+3>0x + 3 > 0x+3>0 and 2x−1>02x - 1 > 02x−1>0, that is x>12x > \frac12x>21​. Equal arguments: x+3=2x−1x + 3 = 2x - 1x+3=2x−1, so x=4x = 4x=4: acceptable.
Example 7.14 With the properties: solutions to discard

log⁡2x+log⁡2(x−2)=3\log_2 x + \log_2(x - 2) = 3log2​x+log2​(x−2)=3.

C.E.: x>0x > 0x>0 and x−2>0x - 2 > 0x−2>0, so x>2x > 2x>2.

With the product property: log⁡2[x(x−2)]=3\log_2[x(x - 2)] = 3log2​[x(x−2)]=3, that is x(x−2)=23=8x(x - 2) = 2^3 = 8x(x−2)=23=8, so x2−2x−8=0x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0x2−2x−8=0, with solutions x=4x = 4x=4 and x=−2x = -2x=−2. Only x=4x = 4x=4 satisfies the C.E. Check: log⁡24+log⁡22=2+1=3\log_2 4 + \log_2 2 = 2 + 1 = 3log2​4+log2​2=2+1=3.

Where does x=−2x = -2x=−2 come from? The expression log⁡2[x(x−2)]\log_2[x(x-2)]log2​[x(x−2)] also exists for x<0x < 0x<0, the original one does not: the transformation enlarged the domain. That is why the C.E. are always written for the initial equation.

Example 7.15 With the quotient property

log⁡2(x+6)−log⁡2x=2\log_2(x + 6) - \log_2 x = 2log2​(x+6)−log2​x=2. C.E.: x+6>0x + 6 > 0x+6>0 and x>0x > 0x>0, so x>0x > 0x>0.

With the quotient property: log⁡2x+6x=2\log_2 \dfrac{x + 6}{x} = 2log2​xx+6​=2, that is x+6x=22=4\dfrac{x + 6}{x} = 2^2 = 4xx+6​=22=4. Multiply by xxx, which is positive: x+6=4xx + 6 = 4xx+6=4x, so x=2x = 2x=2, acceptable. Check: log⁡28−log⁡22=3−1=2\log_2 8 - \log_2 2 = 3 - 1 = 2log2​8−log2​2=3−1=2.

Example 7.16 The C.E. discard the most “natural” solution

log⁡10(x2−9)=log⁡10(3−x)\log_{10}(x^2 - 9) = \log_{10}(3 - x)log10​(x2−9)=log10​(3−x).

C.E.: x2−9>0x^2 - 9 > 0x2−9>0 gives x<−3x < -3x<−3 or x>3x > 3x>3; 3−x>03 - x > 03−x>0 gives x<3x < 3x<3. Together: x<−3x < -3x<−3.

Equal arguments: x2−9=3−xx^2 - 9 = 3 - xx2−9=3−x, that is x2+x−12=0x^2 + x - 12 = 0x2+x−12=0, with solutions x=3x = 3x=3 and x=−4x = -4x=−4. Only x=−4x = -4x=−4 satisfies the C.E.: it is the only solution.

Example 7.17 Substitution

(log⁡2x)2−log⁡2x−2=0(\log_2 x)^2 - \log_2 x - 2 = 0(log2​x)2−log2​x−2=0. C.E.: x>0x > 0x>0. With t=log⁡2xt = \log_2 xt=log2​x: t2−t−2=0t^2 - t - 2 = 0t2−t−2=0, with solutions t=2t = 2t=2 and t=−1t = -1t=−1. So x=22=4x = 2^2 = 4x=22=4 or x=2−1=12x = 2^{-1} = \frac12x=2−1=21​: both acceptable.

Common mistake The logarithm of a square

log⁡3x2=2\log_3 x^2 = 2log3​x2=2. C.E.: x2>0x^2 > 0x2>0, that is x≠0x \neq 0x=0. By the definition x2=9x^2 = 9x2=9, so x=3x = 3x=3 or x=−3x = -3x=−3: two solutions. If you immediately write 2log⁡3x=22\log_3 x = 22log3​x=2 you find only x=3x = 3x=3 and lose x=−3x = -3x=−3, because log⁡3x2=2log⁡3∣x∣\log_3 x^2 = 2\log_3|x|log3​x2=2log3​∣x∣, not 2log⁡3x2\log_3 x2log3​x.

#Exponential inequalities

Rule 7.8 The direction depends on the base
  • If a>1a > 1a>1: af(x)>ag(x)  ⟺  f(x)>g(x)a^{f(x)} > a^{g(x)} \iff f(x) > g(x)af(x)>ag(x)⟺f(x)>g(x) (the direction stays the same).
  • If 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1: af(x)>ag(x)  ⟺  f(x)<g(x)a^{f(x)} > a^{g(x)} \iff f(x) < g(x)af(x)>ag(x)⟺f(x)<g(x) (the direction is reversed).

The same holds with <<<, ≥\geq≥, ≤\leq≤. The reason is monotonicity: with a base greater than 1 the exponential increases, with a base between 0 and 1 it decreases.

Method Solving an exponential inequality
  1. Bring both sides to the same base and compare the exponents, reversing the direction if the base is between 0 and 1.
  2. If one side is a number c≤0c \leq 0c≤0: af(x)>ca^{f(x)} > caf(x)>c is always true (where fff is defined), af(x)<ca^{f(x)} < caf(x)<c is never true. If c>0c > 0c>0, write c=alog⁡acc = a^{\log_a c}c=aloga​c and go back to step 1.
  3. With different bases apply a logarithm with base greater than 1 (for example ln⁡\lnln), which does not change the direction; then, when you divide by the coefficient of xxx, check its sign.
  4. With the substitution t=axt = a^xt=ax solve the inequality in ttt and then go back to xxx.
Example 7.18 Same base
  • 32x−1>3x+23^{2x-1} > 3^{x+2}32x−1>3x+2: base 3>13 > 13>1, the direction stays the same. 2x−1>x+22x - 1 > x + 22x−1>x+2, so x>3x > 3x>3.
  • (12)x−1≥18\left(\frac12\right)^{x-1} \geq \frac18(21​)x−1≥81​: 18=(12)3\frac18 = \left(\frac12\right)^381​=(21​)3 and the base is between 0 and 1, so the direction is reversed: x−1≤3x - 1 \leq 3x−1≤3, hence x≤4x \leq 4x≤4.
  • (13)x<9\left(\frac13\right)^x < 9(31​)x<9: 9=(13)−29 = \left(\frac13\right)^{-2}9=(31​)−2, the direction is reversed: x>−2x > -2x>−2. You reach the same result in base 3: 3−x<323^{-x} < 3^23−x<32, so −x<2-x < 2−x<2, that is x>−2x > -2x>−2.
  • 2x2<2x+22^{x^2} < 2^{x+2}2x2<2x+2: base 2, the direction stays the same: x2<x+2x^2 < x + 2x2<x+2, that is x2−x−2<0x^2 - x - 2 < 0x2−x−2<0. The roots are −1-1−1 and 222 and the parabola is negative between the roots: −1<x<2-1 < x < 2−1<x<2.
Example 7.19 A number on the right-hand side
  • 5x>−15^x > -15x>−1: always true, because 5x5^x5x is positive. Solutions: all of R\RR.
  • ex<0e^x < 0ex<0: never true, no solutions.
  • 3x≤13^x \leq 13x≤1: 1=301 = 3^01=30, so x≤0x \leq 0x≤0.
  • (12)x>3\left(\frac12\right)^x > 3(21​)x>3: apply log⁡1/2\log_{1/2}log1/2​, which reverses the direction: x<log⁡1/23=−log⁡23x < \log_{1/2} 3 = -\log_2 3x<log1/2​3=−log2​3.
Example 7.20 Different bases: watch the sign of the coefficient

2x>3x−12^x > 3^{x-1}2x>3x−1. Apply ln⁡\lnln (base e>1e > 1e>1, the direction stays the same):

xln⁡2>(x−1)ln⁡3  ⇒  xln⁡2−xln⁡3>−ln⁡3  ⇒  x(ln⁡2−ln⁡3)>−ln⁡3x\ln 2 > (x - 1)\ln 3 \;\Rightarrow\; x\ln 2 - x\ln 3 > -\ln 3 \;\Rightarrow\; x(\ln 2 - \ln 3) > -\ln 3xln2>(x−1)ln3⇒xln2−xln3>−ln3⇒x(ln2−ln3)>−ln3

The coefficient ln⁡2−ln⁡3\ln 2 - \ln 3ln2−ln3 is negative (because 2<32 < 32<3): dividing by it reverses the direction.

x<−ln⁡3ln⁡2−ln⁡3=ln⁡3ln⁡3−ln⁡2≈2.71x < \frac{-\ln 3}{\ln 2 - \ln 3} = \frac{\ln 3}{\ln 3 - \ln 2} \approx 2.71x<ln2−ln3−ln3​=ln3−ln2ln3​≈2.71
Example 7.21 Substitution

4x−5⋅2x+4<04^x - 5 \cdot 2^x + 4 < 04x−5⋅2x+4<0. With t=2xt = 2^xt=2x: t2−5t+4<0t^2 - 5t + 4 < 0t2−5t+4<0, with roots 111 and 444, so 1<t<41 < t < 41<t<4. Back to xxx: 1<2x<41 < 2^x < 41<2x<4, that is 20<2x<222^0 < 2^x < 2^220<2x<22, so 0<x<20 < x < 20<x<2.

Common mistake Mistakes in exponential inequalities
  • With a base between 0 and 1 the direction is reversed: this is the most frequent mistake.
  • Dividing by a negative number, such as ln⁡2−ln⁡3\ln 2 - \ln 3ln2−ln3, reverses the direction.
  • 2x>3x2^x > 3^x2x>3x is not “never true”: dividing by 3x>03^x > 03x>0 you get (23)x>1=(23)0\left(\frac23\right)^x > 1 = \left(\frac23\right)^0(32​)x>1=(32​)0 and, with a base between 0 and 1, x<0x < 0x<0. Indeed for x=−1x = -1x=−1: 2−1=0.5>3−1≈0.332^{-1} = 0.5 > 3^{-1} \approx 0.332−1=0.5>3−1≈0.33.

#Logarithmic inequalities

Rule 7.9 Comparing logarithms with the same base

With f(x)>0f(x) > 0f(x)>0 and g(x)>0g(x) > 0g(x)>0:

  • if a>1a > 1a>1: log⁡af(x)>log⁡ag(x)  ⟺  f(x)>g(x)\log_a f(x) > \log_a g(x) \iff f(x) > g(x)loga​f(x)>loga​g(x)⟺f(x)>g(x) (the direction stays the same);
  • if 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1: log⁡af(x)>log⁡ag(x)  ⟺  f(x)<g(x)\log_a f(x) > \log_a g(x) \iff f(x) < g(x)loga​f(x)>loga​g(x)⟺f(x)<g(x) (the direction is reversed).
Method Solving a logarithmic inequality
  1. C.E.: every argument greater than zero.
  2. Write the numbers as logarithms in the same base: c=log⁡aacc = \log_a a^cc=loga​ac (for example 3=log⁡283 = \log_2 83=log2​8 and −1=log⁡1/22-1 = \log_{1/2} 2−1=log1/2​2).
  3. Compare the arguments, reversing the direction if the base is between 0 and 1.
  4. Put the result in a system with the C.E.: they must hold together, so keep only the values they have in common.
Example 7.22 Base greater than 1

log⁡3(x−1)<log⁡3(5−x)\log_3(x - 1) < \log_3(5 - x)log3​(x−1)<log3​(5−x).

C.E.: x−1>0x - 1 > 0x−1>0 and 5−x>05 - x > 05−x>0, that is 1<x<51 < x < 51<x<5.

Base 3>13 > 13>1, the direction stays the same: x−1<5−xx - 1 < 5 - xx−1<5−x, so x<3x < 3x<3.

System with the C.E.: 1<x<31 < x < 31<x<3.

Example 7.23 A number on the right-hand side
  • log⁡2(x+1)≤3\log_2(x + 1) \leq 3log2​(x+1)≤3. C.E.: x>−1x > -1x>−1. Since 3=log⁡283 = \log_2 83=log2​8: x+1≤8x + 1 \leq 8x+1≤8, that is x≤7x \leq 7x≤7. Solutions: −1<x≤7-1 < x \leq 7−1<x≤7, that is the interval (−1,7](-1, 7](−1,7].
  • log⁡1/2(x−2)≥−1\log_{1/2}(x - 2) \geq -1log1/2​(x−2)≥−1. C.E.: x>2x > 2x>2. Since −1=log⁡1/22-1 = \log_{1/2} 2−1=log1/2​2 and the base is between 0 and 1, the direction is reversed: x−2≤2x - 2 \leq 2x−2≤2, that is x≤4x \leq 4x≤4. Solutions: 2<x≤42 < x \leq 42<x≤4.
  • ln⁡(2x−1)<0\ln(2x - 1) < 0ln(2x−1)<0. C.E.: x>12x > \frac12x>21​. Since 0=ln⁡10 = \ln 10=ln1: 2x−1<12x - 1 < 12x−1<1, that is x<1x < 1x<1. Solutions: 12<x<1\frac12 < x < 121​<x<1.
Example 7.24 Solution in two intervals

log⁡10(x2−3x)<1\log_{10}(x^2 - 3x) < 1log10​(x2−3x)<1.

C.E.: x2−3x>0x^2 - 3x > 0x2−3x>0, that is x(x−3)>0x(x - 3) > 0x(x−3)>0: x<0x < 0x<0 or x>3x > 3x>3.

Since 1=log⁡10101 = \log_{10} 101=log10​10: x2−3x<10x^2 - 3x < 10x2−3x<10, that is x2−3x−10<0x^2 - 3x - 10 < 0x2−3x−10<0. The roots are −2-2−2 and 555, so −2<x<5-2 < x < 5−2<x<5.

System: the C.E. and −2<x<5-2 < x < 5−2<x<5 must hold together. You get −2<x<0-2 < x < 0−2<x<0 or 3<x<53 < x < 53<x<5.

Common mistake Mistakes in logarithmic inequalities
  • Without the C.E. you almost always go wrong: the solutions of log⁡2x<3\log_2 x < 3log2​x<3 are not x<8x < 8x<8, but 0<x<80 < x < 80<x<8.
  • Here too, with a base between 0 and 1, the direction is reversed.
  • Watch out for “and” and “or”: the C.E. and the inequality must hold together; the final solution can be made of several pieces, joined by “or”.

#An application: pH

In chemistry the acidity of a solution is measured by its pH:

pH=−log⁡10[H+]\mathrm{pH} = -\log_{10}[\mathrm{H}^+]pH=−log10​[H+]

where [H+][\mathrm{H}^+][H+] is the concentration of hydrogen ions. If pH<7\mathrm{pH} < 7pH<7 the solution is acidic, if pH>7\mathrm{pH} > 7pH>7 it is basic.

  • [H+]=10−3[\mathrm{H}^+] = 10^{-3}[H+]=10−3 gives pH=−log⁡1010−3=3\mathrm{pH} = -\log_{10} 10^{-3} = 3pH=−log10​10−3=3: acidic solution.
  • If pH=9\mathrm{pH} = 9pH=9, then log⁡10[H+]=−9\log_{10}[\mathrm{H}^+] = -9log10​[H+]=−9 and [H+]=10−9[\mathrm{H}^+] = 10^{-9}[H+]=10−9: basic solution.
  • One pH unit less means a concentration 10 times larger; two units less, 100 times larger.
Example 7.25 From pH to concentration

A solution has pH=4.5\mathrm{pH} = 4.5pH=4.5. Call xxx the concentration: −log⁡10x=4.5-\log_{10} x = 4.5−log10​x=4.5, that is log⁡10x=−4.5\log_{10} x = -4.5log10​x=−4.5. By the definition of logarithm:

x=10−4.5=100.5⋅10−5=10⋅10−5≈3.16⋅10−5x = 10^{-4.5} = 10^{0.5} \cdot 10^{-5} = \sqrt{10} \cdot 10^{-5} \approx 3.16 \cdot 10^{-5}x=10−4.5=100.5⋅10−5=10​⋅10−5≈3.16⋅10−5

And when is a solution acidic? pH<7\mathrm{pH} < 7pH<7 means −log⁡10x<7-\log_{10} x < 7−log10​x<7, that is log⁡10x>−7\log_{10} x > -7log10​x>−7 (multiplying by −1-1−1 reverses the direction), so x>10−7x > 10^{-7}x>10−7.

In the test Equations and inequalities in the test questions
  • Equations: it is often faster to substitute the options into the equation than to solve it. First of all, discard the options that do not satisfy the domain conditions.
  • Inequalities: try a convenient value (such as x=0x = 0x=0 or x=1x = 1x=1) in the original inequality and eliminate the options that treat it the wrong way. Then look at the endpoints: they are excluded if the C.E. or the strict sign require it.
  • Mistakes to avoid: the direction not reversed with a base between 0 and 1, forgotten C.E., values of ttt mistaken for solutions. Also remember that the same solution can be written in different forms: log⁡3/22\log_{3/2} 2log3/2​2 and ln⁡2ln⁡3−ln⁡2\frac{\ln 2}{\ln 3 - \ln 2}ln3−ln2ln2​ are the same number.
  • Numeric answer: without a calculator a number like log⁡37\log_3 7log3​7 cannot be turned into a decimal. If a question that asks for a number leads you there, recheck your steps.

#Exercises

Exercise 7.1BasicComputing logarithms

Compute without a calculator:

  • log⁡232\log_2 32log2​32
  • log⁡3127\log_3 \frac{1}{27}log3​271​
  • log⁡1/216\log_{1/2} 16log1/2​16
  • log⁡255\log_{25} 5log25​5
  • log⁡100.001\log_{10} 0.001log10​0.001
  • log⁡84\log_8 4log8​4
Solution

For each one, look for the exponent you must give the base to obtain the argument.

  • 32=2532 = 2^532=25, so log⁡232=5\log_2 32 = 5log2​32=5.
  • 127=3−3\frac{1}{27} = 3^{-3}271​=3−3, so log⁡3127=−3\log_3 \frac{1}{27} = -3log3​271​=−3.
  • 16=24=(12)−416 = 2^4 = \left(\frac12\right)^{-4}16=24=(21​)−4, so log⁡1/216=−4\log_{1/2} 16 = -4log1/2​16=−4.
  • 5=25=251/25 = \sqrt{25} = 25^{1/2}5=25​=251/2, so log⁡255=12\log_{25} 5 = \frac12log25​5=21​.
  • 0.001=11000=10−30.001 = \frac{1}{1000} = 10^{-3}0.001=10001​=10−3, so log⁡100.001=−3\log_{10} 0.001 = -3log10​0.001=−3.
  • 8=238 = 2^38=23 and 4=224 = 2^24=22, so log⁡84=23\log_8 4 = \frac{2}{3}log8​4=32​. Check: 82/3=(83)2=22=48^{2/3} = \left(\sqrt[3]{8}\right)^2 = 2^2 = 482/3=(38​)2=22=4.
Exercise 7.2BasicPowers with fractional and negative exponents

Compute: 163/416^{3/4}163/4,   27−2/3\;27^{-2/3}27−2/3,   (49)−1/2\;\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)^{-1/2}(94​)−1/2,   23⋅4−1⋅81/3\;2^3 \cdot 4^{-1} \cdot 8^{1/3}23⋅4−1⋅81/3.

Solution
  • 163/4=(164)3=23=816^{3/4} = \left(\sqrt[4]{16}\right)^3 = 2^3 = 8163/4=(416​)3=23=8.
  • 27−2/3=1(273)2=132=1927^{-2/3} = \dfrac{1}{\left(\sqrt[3]{27}\right)^2} = \dfrac{1}{3^2} = \dfrac{1}{9}27−2/3=(327​)21​=321​=91​.
  • (49)−1/2=(94)1/2=94=32\left(\frac{4}{9}\right)^{-1/2} = \left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{1/2} = \sqrt{\frac94} = \frac{3}{2}(94​)−1/2=(49​)1/2=49​​=23​.
  • Everything in base 2: 4−1=2−24^{-1} = 2^{-2}4−1=2−2 and 81/3=83=28^{1/3} = \sqrt[3]{8} = 281/3=38​=2. So 23⋅2−2⋅21=23−2+1=22=42^3 \cdot 2^{-2} \cdot 2^1 = 2^{3 - 2 + 1} = 2^2 = 423⋅2−2⋅21=23−2+1=22=4.
Exercise 7.3BasicOrdering without a calculator

Put in order from smallest to largest: 2−12^{-1}2−1,   20.5\;2^{0.5}20.5,   (12)−2\;\left(\frac12\right)^{-2}(21​)−2,   40\;4^040.

Solution

Write everything as a power of 2: (12)−2=22\left(\frac12\right)^{-2} = 2^2(21​)−2=22 and 40=1=204^0 = 1 = 2^040=1=20. Now you have 2−12^{-1}2−1, 20.52^{0.5}20.5, 222^222, 202^020.

The base 2 is greater than 1: the power with the larger exponent is the larger one. The exponents in order are −1<0<0.5<2-1 < 0 < 0.5 < 2−1<0<0.5<2, so

2−1<40<20.5<(12)−22^{-1} < 4^0 < 2^{0.5} < \left(\frac12\right)^{-2}2−1<40<20.5<(21​)−2

that is 0.5<1<2<40.5 < 1 < \sqrt{2} < 40.5<1<2​<4 (with 2≈1.41\sqrt2 \approx 1.412​≈1.41).

Exercise 7.4BasicElementary exponential equations

Solve: 3x+1=273^{x+1} = 273x+1=27,   52x=15\;5^{2x} = \frac{1}{5}52x=51​,   2x=−8\;2^x = -82x=−8,   7x−2=1\;7^{x-2} = 17x−2=1.

Solution
  • 27=3327 = 3^327=33, so x+1=3x + 1 = 3x+1=3 and x=2x = 2x=2.
  • 15=5−1\frac15 = 5^{-1}51​=5−1, so 2x=−12x = -12x=−1 and x=−12x = -\frac12x=−21​.
  • 2x2^x2x is always positive and cannot equal −8-8−8: the equation is impossible.
  • 1=701 = 7^01=70, so x−2=0x - 2 = 0x−2=0 and x=2x = 2x=2.
Exercise 7.5BasicElementary logarithmic equations

Solve: log⁡2(3x−1)=3\log_2(3x - 1) = 3log2​(3x−1)=3 and log⁡5(x+4)=log⁡5(2x+1)\log_5(x + 4) = \log_5(2x + 1)log5​(x+4)=log5​(2x+1).

Solution

First equation. C.E.: 3x−1>03x - 1 > 03x−1>0, that is x>13x > \frac13x>31​. By the definition of logarithm 3x−1=23=83x - 1 = 2^3 = 83x−1=23=8, so 3x=93x = 93x=9 and x=3x = 3x=3. Since 3>133 > \frac133>31​, the solution is acceptable.

Second equation. C.E.: x+4>0x + 4 > 0x+4>0 and 2x+1>02x + 1 > 02x+1>0, that is x>−4x > -4x>−4 and x>−12x > -\frac12x>−21​: together, x>−12x > -\frac12x>−21​. Equal arguments: x+4=2x+1x + 4 = 2x + 1x+4=2x+1, so x=3x = 3x=3, acceptable. Check: log⁡57=log⁡57\log_5 7 = \log_5 7log5​7=log5​7.

Exercise 7.6IntermediateExpanding and combining

Expand log⁡28a3b\log_2 \dfrac{8a^3}{\sqrt{b}}log2​b​8a3​ (with a>0a > 0a>0 and b>0b > 0b>0). Then write 2ln⁡x−ln⁡(x+1)+ln⁡32\ln x - \ln(x + 1) + \ln 32lnx−ln(x+1)+ln3 (with x>0x > 0x>0) as a single logarithm.

Solution

Expanding. Quotient, then product, then powers (b=b1/2\sqrt{b} = b^{1/2}b​=b1/2):

log⁡28a3b=log⁡28+log⁡2a3−log⁡2b1/2=3+3log⁡2a−12log⁡2b\log_2 \frac{8a^3}{\sqrt{b}} = \log_2 8 + \log_2 a^3 - \log_2 b^{1/2} = 3 + 3\log_2 a - \frac{1}{2}\log_2 blog2​b​8a3​=log2​8+log2​a3−log2​b1/2=3+3log2​a−21​log2​b

2ln⁡x−ln⁡(x+1)+ln⁡3=ln⁡x2+ln⁡3−ln⁡(x+1)=ln⁡3x2x+12\ln x - \ln(x + 1) + \ln 3 = \ln x^2 + \ln 3 - \ln(x + 1) = \ln \frac{3x^2}{x + 1}2lnx−ln(x+1)+ln3=lnx2+ln3−ln(x+1)=lnx+13x2​
Exercise 7.7IntermediateComputing with the properties

Compute: log⁡612+log⁡63\log_6 12 + \log_6 3log6​12+log6​3,   log⁡354−log⁡32\;\log_3 54 - \log_3 2log3​54−log3​2,   log⁡927\;\log_9 27log9​27,   log⁡23⋅log⁡316\;\log_2 3 \cdot \log_3 16log2​3⋅log3​16.

Solution
  • Product: log⁡612+log⁡63=log⁡636=2\log_6 12 + \log_6 3 = \log_6 36 = 2log6​12+log6​3=log6​36=2.
  • Quotient: log⁡354−log⁡32=log⁡327=3\log_3 54 - \log_3 2 = \log_3 27 = 3log3​54−log3​2=log3​27=3.
  • Change of base, to base 3: log⁡927=log⁡327log⁡39=32\log_9 27 = \dfrac{\log_3 27}{\log_3 9} = \dfrac{3}{2}log9​27=log3​9log3​27​=23​.
  • Change of base, to base eee: log⁡23⋅log⁡316=ln⁡3ln⁡2⋅ln⁡16ln⁡3=ln⁡16ln⁡2=log⁡216=4\log_2 3 \cdot \log_3 16 = \dfrac{\ln 3}{\ln 2} \cdot \dfrac{\ln 16}{\ln 3} = \dfrac{\ln 16}{\ln 2} = \log_2 16 = 4log2​3⋅log3​16=ln2ln3​⋅ln3ln16​=ln2ln16​=log2​16=4.
Exercise 7.8IntermediateTaking out a common power

Solve 3x+1+3x−1=303^{x+1} + 3^{x-1} = 303x+1+3x−1=30.

Solution

Write the two powers as multiples of 3x3^x3x: 3x+1=3⋅3x3^{x+1} = 3 \cdot 3^x3x+1=3⋅3x and 3x−1=13⋅3x3^{x-1} = \frac13 \cdot 3^x3x−1=31​⋅3x. Take out the common factor:

3x(3+13)=30  ⇒  3x⋅103=30  ⇒  3x=9  ⇒  x=23^x\left(3 + \frac{1}{3}\right) = 30 \;\Rightarrow\; 3^x \cdot \frac{10}{3} = 30 \;\Rightarrow\; 3^x = 9 \;\Rightarrow\; x = 23x(3+31​)=30⇒3x⋅310​=30⇒3x=9⇒x=2

Check: 33+31=27+3=303^3 + 3^1 = 27 + 3 = 3033+31=27+3=30.

Exercise 7.9IntermediateLogarithmic equation with the product

Solve log⁡3x+log⁡3(x+6)=3\log_3 x + \log_3(x + 6) = 3log3​x+log3​(x+6)=3.

Solution

C.E.: x>0x > 0x>0 and x+6>0x + 6 > 0x+6>0; together, x>0x > 0x>0.

With the product property: log⁡3[x(x+6)]=3\log_3[x(x + 6)] = 3log3​[x(x+6)]=3, so x(x+6)=33=27x(x + 6) = 3^3 = 27x(x+6)=33=27, that is x2+6x−27=0x^2 + 6x - 27 = 0x2+6x−27=0. It factorises: (x+9)(x−3)=0(x + 9)(x - 3) = 0(x+9)(x−3)=0, so x=−9x = -9x=−9 or x=3x = 3x=3.

x=−9x = -9x=−9 does not satisfy the C.E. and is discarded. The only solution is x=3x = 3x=3. Check: log⁡33+log⁡39=1+2=3\log_3 3 + \log_3 9 = 1 + 2 = 3log3​3+log3​9=1+2=3.

Exercise 7.10IntermediateOne exponential, one logarithmic

Solve: (12)2x−3>18\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2x - 3} > \frac{1}{8}(21​)2x−3>81​ and log⁡2(x−3)≤2\log_2(x - 3) \leq 2log2​(x−3)≤2.

Solution

First. 18=(12)3\frac18 = \left(\frac12\right)^381​=(21​)3, so (12)2x−3>(12)3\left(\frac12\right)^{2x-3} > \left(\frac12\right)^3(21​)2x−3>(21​)3. The base is between 0 and 1: the direction is reversed, 2x−3<32x - 3 < 32x−3<3, that is x<3x < 3x<3.

Second. C.E.: x>3x > 3x>3. Since 2=log⁡242 = \log_2 42=log2​4 and the base is greater than 1: x−3≤4x - 3 \leq 4x−3≤4, that is x≤7x \leq 7x≤7. System with the C.E.: 3<x≤73 < x \leq 73<x≤7, that is the interval (3,7](3, 7](3,7].

Exercise 7.11IntermediateBase between 0 and 1

Solve log⁡1/3(2x−1)>−2\log_{1/3}(2x - 1) > -2log1/3​(2x−1)>−2.

Solution

C.E.: 2x−1>02x - 1 > 02x−1>0, that is x>12x > \frac12x>21​.

Write −2-2−2 as a logarithm to base 13\frac1331​: −2=log⁡1/3(13)−2=log⁡1/39-2 = \log_{1/3}\left(\frac13\right)^{-2} = \log_{1/3} 9−2=log1/3​(31​)−2=log1/3​9. The inequality becomes log⁡1/3(2x−1)>log⁡1/39\log_{1/3}(2x - 1) > \log_{1/3} 9log1/3​(2x−1)>log1/3​9. The base is between 0 and 1, so the direction is reversed:

2x−1<9  ⇒  x<52x - 1 < 9 \;\Rightarrow\; x < 52x−1<9⇒x<5

System with the C.E.: 12<x<5\frac12 < x < 521​<x<5.

Exercise 7.12Test levelSubstitution

The equation 9x−4⋅3x+3=09^x - 4 \cdot 3^x + 3 = 09x−4⋅3x+3=0: how many solutions does it have and what is their sum?

Solution

Since 9x=(3x)29^x = \left(3^x\right)^29x=(3x)2, set t=3xt = 3^xt=3x (with t>0t > 0t>0): t2−4t+3=0t^2 - 4t + 3 = 0t2−4t+3=0, with solutions t=1t = 1t=1 and t=3t = 3t=3, both positive.

Back to xxx: 3x=13^x = 13x=1 gives x=0x = 0x=0; 3x=33^x = 33x=3 gives x=1x = 1x=1. There are two solutions and their sum is 0+1=10 + 1 = 10+1=1.

Careful: 4 is the sum of the values of ttt, not of the solutions in xxx.

Exercise 7.13Test levelAn inequality in two pieces

Solve log⁡2(x2−4x)<5\log_2(x^2 - 4x) < 5log2​(x2−4x)<5.

Solution

C.E.: x2−4x>0x^2 - 4x > 0x2−4x>0, that is x(x−4)>0x(x - 4) > 0x(x−4)>0: x<0x < 0x<0 or x>4x > 4x>4.

Since 5=log⁡2325 = \log_2 325=log2​32 and the base is greater than 1: x2−4x<32x^2 - 4x < 32x2−4x<32, that is x2−4x−32<0x^2 - 4x - 32 < 0x2−4x−32<0. It factorises: (x−8)(x+4)<0(x - 8)(x + 4) < 0(x−8)(x+4)<0, true between the roots: −4<x<8-4 < x < 8−4<x<8.

System with the C.E.: −4<x<0-4 < x < 0−4<x<0 or 4<x<84 < x < 84<x<8.

Exercise 7.14Test levelDifferent bases and an estimate

Solve 2x+1=5x2^{x+1} = 5^x2x+1=5x and determine between which two consecutive integers the solution lies.

Solution

Apply ln⁡\lnln to both sides: (x+1)ln⁡2=xln⁡5(x + 1)\ln 2 = x\ln 5(x+1)ln2=xln5, so ln⁡2=x(ln⁡5−ln⁡2)\ln 2 = x(\ln 5 - \ln 2)ln2=x(ln5−ln2) and

x=ln⁡2ln⁡5−ln⁡2=ln⁡2ln⁡52x = \frac{\ln 2}{\ln 5 - \ln 2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\ln \frac{5}{2}}x=ln5−ln2ln2​=ln25​ln2​

Alternatively: divide both sides by 2x2^x2x and you get 2=(52)x2 = \left(\frac52\right)^x2=(25​)x, that is x=log⁡5/22x = \log_{5/2} 2x=log5/2​2.

Estimate: (52)0=1<2<52=(52)1\left(\frac52\right)^0 = 1 < 2 < \frac52 = \left(\frac52\right)^1(25​)0=1<2<25​=(25​)1 and the base 52\frac5225​ is greater than 1, so the exponent you are looking for lies between 0 and 1: 0<x<10 < x < 10<x<1 (it is about 0.760.760.76).

Exercise 7.15Test levelGrowth of a colony

A colony of bacteria doubles every 3 hours. At 8:00 in the morning there are 500 bacteria. At what time will there be 8000?

Solution

After ttt hours the colony has doubled t3\frac{t}{3}3t​ times, so N(t)=500⋅2t/3N(t) = 500 \cdot 2^{t/3}N(t)=500⋅2t/3. Set N(t)=8000N(t) = 8000N(t)=8000:

500⋅2t/3=8000  ⇒  2t/3=16=24  ⇒  t3=4  ⇒  t=12500 \cdot 2^{t/3} = 8000 \;\Rightarrow\; 2^{t/3} = 16 = 2^4 \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{t}{3} = 4 \;\Rightarrow\; t = 12500⋅2t/3=8000⇒2t/3=16=24⇒3t​=4⇒t=12

Twelve hours after 8:00 in the morning: at 20:00.

Exercise 7.16Test levelA rational inequality with an exponential

Solve 3x−9x+1≥0\dfrac{3^x - 9}{x + 1} \geq 0x+13x−9​≥0.

Solution

C.E.: x+1≠0x + 1 \neq 0x+1=0, that is x≠−1x \neq -1x=−1.

Study the sign of the two pieces:

  • numerator: 3x−9≥03^x - 9 \geq 03x−9≥0 when 3x≥323^x \geq 3^23x≥32, that is x≥2x \geq 2x≥2;
  • denominator: x+1>0x + 1 > 0x+1>0 when x>−1x > -1x>−1.

Sign chart: for x<−1x < -1x<−1 numerator negative and denominator negative, fraction positive; for −1<x<2-1 < x < 2−1<x<2 numerator negative and denominator positive, fraction negative; for x>2x > 2x>2 fraction positive. At x=2x = 2x=2 the numerator is zero and so is the fraction: with ≥\geq≥ the value x=2x = 2x=2 is accepted.

Solutions: x<−1x < -1x<−1 or x≥2x \geq 2x≥2.

Exercise 7.17Test levelWatch out for the square

How many solutions does the equation ln⁡(x2)=ln⁡(x+6)\ln(x^2) = \ln(x + 6)ln(x2)=ln(x+6) have?

Solution

C.E.: x2>0x^2 > 0x2>0, that is x≠0x \neq 0x=0, and x+6>0x + 6 > 0x+6>0, that is x>−6x > -6x>−6.

Equal arguments: x2=x+6x^2 = x + 6x2=x+6, that is x2−x−6=0x^2 - x - 6 = 0x2−x−6=0, which factorises as (x−3)(x+2)=0(x - 3)(x + 2) = 0(x−3)(x+2)=0: x=3x = 3x=3 or x=−2x = -2x=−2.

Both satisfy the C.E. (for x=−2x = -2x=−2: x2=4>0x^2 = 4 > 0x2=4>0 and x+6=4>0x + 6 = 4 > 0x+6=4>0). There are two solutions. If you turn ln⁡(x2)\ln(x^2)ln(x2) into 2ln⁡x2\ln x2lnx you impose x>0x > 0x>0 and lose x=−2x = -2x=−2.

#Self-check quiz

  1. What is the value of log⁡3181\log_3 \dfrac{1}{81}log3​811​?
    -4
    181=134=3−4\dfrac{1}{81} = \dfrac{1}{3^4} = 3^{-4}811​=341​=3−4, so the exponent to give 3 is −4-4−4.
  2. What is the value of log⁡224−log⁡23\log_2 24 - \log_2 3log2​24−log2​3?
    3
    The difference of two logarithms with the same base is the logarithm of the quotient: log⁡2243=log⁡28=3\log_2 \dfrac{24}{3} = \log_2 8 = 3log2​324​=log2​8=3.
  3. What is the domain of the function f(x)=ln⁡(9−x2)f(x) = \ln(9 - x^2)f(x)=ln(9−x2)?
    You need 9−x2>09 - x^2 > 09−x2>0, that is x2<9x^2 < 9x2<9, so −3<x<3-3 < x < 3−3<x<3. The endpoints are excluded because the argument must be strictly positive (ln⁡0\ln 0ln0 does not exist). (0,3)(0, 3)(0,3) comes from confusing the condition on the argument with x>0x > 0x>0; (−∞,−3)∪(3,+∞)(-\infty, -3) \cup (3, +\infty)(−∞,−3)∪(3,+∞), on the other hand, is the set where 9−x29 - x^29−x2 is negative.
  4. True or false: log⁡2(x+y)=log⁡2x+log⁡2y\log_2(x + y) = \log_2 x + \log_2 ylog2​(x+y)=log2​x+log2​y holds for every x>0x > 0x>0 and y>0y > 0y>0.
    There is no rule at all for the sum. Counterexample: log⁡2(4+4)=log⁡28=3\log_2(4 + 4) = \log_2 8 = 3log2​(4+4)=log2​8=3, while log⁡24+log⁡24=2+2=4\log_2 4 + \log_2 4 = 2 + 2 = 4log2​4+log2​4=2+2=4. The true rule concerns the product: log⁡2(xy)=log⁡2x+log⁡2y\log_2(xy) = \log_2 x + \log_2 ylog2​(xy)=log2​x+log2​y.
  5. True or false: 22<21.52^{\sqrt{2}} < 2^{1.5}22​<21.5.
    The base 2 is greater than 1, so the power with the larger exponent is the larger one. Since 1.52=2.25>21.5^2 = 2.25 > 21.52=2.25>2, we have 2<1.5\sqrt{2} < 1.52​<1.5 and therefore 22<21.52^{\sqrt 2} < 2^{1.5}22​<21.5.
  6. Let f(x)=axf(x) = a^xf(x)=ax with 0<a<10 < a < 10<a<1. Which statements are true?
    One or more correct answers
    Every exponential equals 1 at x=0x = 0x=0 and is always positive. With a base between 0 and 1 the function is decreasing, so a larger xxx corresponds to a smaller value: f(2)>f(3)f(2) > f(3)f(2)>f(3). The domain is all of R\RR; (0,+∞)(0, +\infty)(0,+∞) is the range.
  7. Solve the equation 4x=84^x = 84x=8. What is the value of xxx?
    3/2
    Write everything in base 2: 22x=232^{2x} = 2^322x=23, so 2x=32x = 32x=3 and x=32x = \dfrac{3}{2}x=23​.
  8. What are the solutions of the equation log⁡3x+log⁡3(x−8)=2\log_3 x + \log_3(x - 8) = 2log3​x+log3​(x−8)=2?
    Domain conditions: x>0x > 0x>0 and x>8x > 8x>8, so x>8x > 8x>8. Then log⁡3[x(x−8)]=2\log_3[x(x - 8)] = 2log3​[x(x−8)]=2 gives x2−8x=9x^2 - 8x = 9x2−8x=9, that is x2−8x−9=0x^2 - 8x - 9 = 0x2−8x−9=0, with roots 999 and −1-1−1. Only x=9x = 9x=9 satisfies the domain conditions.
  9. The solution set of (13)x−2>9\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x-2} > 9(31​)x−2>9 is
    9=(13)−29 = \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{-2}9=(31​)−2, so the inequality is (13)x−2>(13)−2\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{x-2} > \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{-2}(31​)x−2>(31​)−2. The base is between 0 and 1 and the direction is reversed: x−2<−2x - 2 < -2x−2<−2, that is x<0x < 0x<0. If you do not reverse the direction you find x>0x > 0x>0; if you wrongly write 9=(13)29 = \left(\frac13\right)^29=(31​)2 you find x<4x < 4x<4 (or x>4x > 4x>4 if you also get the direction wrong).
  10. The solution set of log⁡1/2(x−1)>1\log_{1/2}(x - 1) > 1log1/2​(x−1)>1 is
    Domain condition: x>1x > 1x>1. Then 1=log⁡1/2121 = \log_{1/2} \dfrac{1}{2}1=log1/2​21​ and, with a base between 0 and 1, the direction is reversed: x−1<12x - 1 < \dfrac{1}{2}x−1<21​, that is x<32x < \dfrac{3}{2}x<23​. Together with the condition x>1x > 1x>1 you get 1<x<321 < x < \dfrac321<x<23​. The answer x<32x < \frac32x<23​ forgets the domain conditions, x>32x > \frac32x>23​ forgets to reverse the direction.
  11. Which equalities hold for every x>0x > 0x>0?
    One or more correct answers
    The three true equalities are the product and reciprocal properties: ln⁡(e2x)=ln⁡e2+ln⁡x\ln(e^2x) = \ln e^2 + \ln xln(e2x)=lne2+lnx and log⁡2(8x)=log⁡28+log⁡2x\log_2(8x) = \log_2 8 + \log_2 xlog2​(8x)=log2​8+log2​x. On the other hand, ln⁡(x2)=2ln⁡x\ln(x^2) = 2\ln xln(x2)=2lnx, which for x=ex = ex=e equals 2, while (ln⁡e)2=1(\ln e)^2 = 1(lne)2=1; and log⁡2(x+8)\log_2(x + 8)log2​(x+8) does not split: for x=8x = 8x=8 it equals 4, while log⁡28+3=6\log_2 8 + 3 = 6log2​8+3=6.
  12. What is the value of 23+log⁡252^{3 + \log_2 5}23+log2​5?
    40
    23+log⁡25=23⋅2log⁡25=8⋅5=402^{3 + \log_2 5} = 2^3 \cdot 2^{\log_2 5} = 8 \cdot 5 = 4023+log2​5=23⋅2log2​5=8⋅5=40, because alog⁡ax=xa^{\log_a x} = xaloga​x=x.
  13. The graph of y=log⁡axy = \log_a xy=loga​x passes through the point (9,2)(9, 2)(9,2). What is the value of the base aaa?
    The point (9,2)(9, 2)(9,2) on the graph means log⁡a9=2\log_a 9 = 2loga​9=2, that is a2=9a^2 = 9a2=9. The base must be positive, so a=3a = 3a=3. a=81a = 81a=81 comes from 929^292 (roles of base and argument swapped), 92\frac9229​ from dividing instead of using the definition, −3-3−3 is not an allowed base.
  14. True or false: the equation 5x=−255^x = -255x=−25 has the solution x=−2x = -2x=−2.
    5−2=1255^{-2} = \dfrac{1}{25}5−2=251​, not −25-25−25. An exponential with a positive base is always positive, so 5x=−255^x = -255x=−25 is impossible.
  15. A solution has [H+]=10−4[\mathrm{H}^+] = 10^{-4}[H+]=10−4. Another one has a concentration of hydrogen ions 100 times smaller. What is the pH of the second solution?
    The second concentration is 10−4100=10−4⋅10−2=10−6\dfrac{10^{-4}}{100} = 10^{-4} \cdot 10^{-2} = 10^{-6}10010−4​=10−4⋅10−2=10−6, so pH=−log⁡1010−6=6\mathrm{pH} = -\log_{10} 10^{-6} = 6pH=−log10​10−6=6. A smaller concentration gives a higher pH (a less acidic solution). −6-6−6 comes from forgetting the minus sign in the definition, 222 from subtracting instead of adding.
  16. Which numbers are solutions of 4x−5⋅2x+4=04^x - 5 \cdot 2^x + 4 = 04x−5⋅2x+4=0?
    One or more correct answers
    With t=2xt = 2^xt=2x the equation becomes t2−5t+4=0t^2 - 5t + 4 = 0t2−5t+4=0, with solutions t=1t = 1t=1 and t=4t = 4t=4. Going back to xxx: 2x=12^x = 12x=1 gives x=0x = 0x=0 and 2x=42^x = 42x=4 gives x=2x = 2x=2. The numbers 1 and 4 are the values of ttt, not of xxx.
